sources.method: CSO Table 2.4, people aged 15 to 64 and 65+. NI total less ages 0 to 14 less 65+, not the pension-age definition. Annual CSO interpolation is ours. Budget 2027 Table 18 debt ratios mapped to model years 1 to 4, then last ratio held. Apply ratios to model real GNI*, not nominal debt stocks.

equations.euSupport: NI reference output * selected peak share * ramp, hold and five-year run-off
equations.trade: Current NI output * (selected border gain * unremoved Windsor share - selected GB loss) * phase
equations.fdi: Additional jobs above current NI intensity * real output or receipts per job. Republic displacement deducted. No second marginal tax on FDI output.
equations.integration: One-off implementation spending less phased savings. Saving requires positive implementation cost.
equations.income: Not calculated. GDP is neither augmented nor reduced by fiscal transfers to manufacture household earned income.
equations.island: Only the capital, trade and net FDI channel terms. The assumed growth gap and other residual differences are recorded separately and cannot pass an economic test.
equations.capital: Output difference holding chosen growth and all other settings fixed, removing programme and EU-funded capital only.
equations.reconciliation: Total output difference = assumed growth gap + capital + trade + net FDI + other output differences.
equations.direction: Current strict rule includes the change from year 19 to 20, followed by a fall in every later year. Interpretation remains an open decision.
equations.debt: Budget 2027 debt ratio schedule applied to unchanged model real GNI* baseline, plus transition borrowing. Divide by scenario Republic GNI*.
equations.demography: People 65+ / people aged 15 to 64. NI annual source and linearly interpolated CSO knots.

limitations: Only three fiscal checks are scored. Household earned income remains unavailable and no overall favourable classification is reported.
Baseline debt ratios are a scenario overlay. Budget years 2027 to 2030 index model years 1 to 4, while demographic normalisation stays 2024. Not a calendar-year forecast.
An 80% ceiling is Stephen’s assessment choice, not an established safe debt limit.

The four-of-five rule is reserved for future use after economic tests can be measured. The annual burden limit is 2% of Republic GNI* with 1% and 3% sensitivities. These are assessment choices, not empirical safety limits.
The low-growth comparison uses a selected 1.3% illustration, not a verified historical estimate.
No empirical central values have been supplied for new trade, FDI or integration effects. These remain off in public controls.
EU grant allocation finances already-costed programme investment. It cannot create a second capital stock for the same spending.
Core policy growth is growth from other causes whenever separately modelled benefits are enabled. No causal growth premium is attached automatically to constitutional form.
The UK does not necessarily save the entire allocated transfer. Retained pension obligations, debt and UK-specific allocations remain distinct.
FDI employment and output are additive illustrations. No complete labour market, tax reform, general-equilibrium displacement or profit repatriation account is estimated.
